source: Home Ustav (1910): fasts (fol. 9-30), prayer at home (ch. 4) and the dismissals for the whole year (fol. 226-253); English translation

prayers.title: The Entrance Opening
prayers.content:
O God, be merciful to me a sinner. (prostration)

Thou who hast created me, O Lord, have mercy on me. (prostration)

Without number have I sinned; O Lord, have mercy, and forgive me a sinner. (prostration)

It is truly meet to bless thee, O God-bearer, ever blessed and most immaculate, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify.

A great prostration. This one is never left out.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. (prostration)

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless. (prostration)

Then the dismissal:

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of Saint N., whose church this is, and of the holy angel my guardian, and of all thy saints: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me and save me, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

All these prostrations are made to the ground, except on Saturdays, Sundays and feast days. Likewise, throughout Pentecost and during the twelve days after Christ's Nativity, they are made as waist bows.

prayers.title: The Departing Opening
prayers.content:
The departing opening, made in the same way as the entrance opening:

O God, be merciful to me a sinner. (prostration)

Thou who hast created me, O Lord, have mercy on me. (prostration)

Without number have I sinned; O Lord, have mercy, and forgive me a sinner. (prostration)

It is truly meet to bless thee, O God-bearer, ever blessed and most immaculate, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify.

A great prostration. This one is never left out.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. (prostration)

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless. (prostration)

Then the dismissal:

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of Saint N., whose church this is, and of the holy angel my guardian, and of all thy saints: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me and save me, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Through the prayers of our holy fathers
prayers.content: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us. Amen.

prayers.title: O Heavenly King
prayers.content: O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and dwell in us, and cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One.

prayers.title: Trisagion through the Our Father
prayers.content:
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. (three times, with three prostrations)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O most holy Trinity, have mercy on us. O Lord, cleanse our sins. O Master, pardon our iniquities. O Holy One, visit and heal our infirmities, for thy name's sake.

Lord, have mercy. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us. Amen.

prayers.title: Glory, both now
prayers.content: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: O come, let us worship
prayers.content:
O come, let us worship God our King.

O come, let us worship Christ, our King and God.

O come, let us worship and fall down before the Lord Jesus Christ himself, our King and God.

Three prostrations.

prayers.title: Glory to thee, our God, for all things
prayers.content: Glory to thee, our God, glory to thee for all things. (three times)

prayers.title: Prayer of St Macarius, with three prostrations
prayers.content:
Make three prostrations, saying the prayer of Saint Macarius:

O God, cleanse me a sinner, for I have never done any good thing before thee. (prostration)

But deliver me from the evil one, and let thy will be done in me. (prostration)

That without condemnation I may open my unworthy mouth, and praise thy holy name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

prayers.title: Prayer: Having risen from sleep
prayers.content:
Prayer.

Having risen from sleep, I give thanks unto thee, O all-holy Trinity, that for thy great goodness and longsuffering thou hast not been angry with me, a sinner and slothful servant, neither hast thou destroyed me with mine iniquities, but hast shown thy love toward mankind; and when I lay in hopelessness, thou hast raised me up to keep the morning watch and to glorify thine invincible dominion. And now, O Master, God most holy, enlighten the eyes of my heart, and open my lips to learn of thy words, and to understand thy commandments, and to do thy will, and to sing unto thee in the confession of my heart, and to hymn and glorify thine all-honorable and majestic name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: The Creed
prayers.content:
I believe in one God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God, begotten, but not made; of one essence with the Father, by whom all things were made. Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Ghost and the Virgin Mary, and was made man. And was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried. And rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures. And ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; of whose kingdom there is no end.

Of the Second Council.

And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord, the true and life-giving, who proceedeth from the Father; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spake by the prophets. In one holy catholic and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come. Amen.

prayers.title: Alleluia, glory to thee, O God
prayers.content: Alleluia, alleluia, glory to thee, O God. (three times, with three prostrations)

prayers.title: The Jesus Prayer
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me a sinner.

prayers.title: Ending: More honorable, with prostrations
prayers.content:
More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify. (prostration)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. (prostration)

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless. (prostration)

prayers.title: Ending: It is truly meet, with prostrations
prayers.content:
It is truly meet to bless thee, O God-bearer, ever blessed and most immaculate, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify. (a great prostration)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. (prostration)

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless. (prostration)

prayers.title: Ending: Glory, both now, with prostrations
prayers.content:
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. (prostration)

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen. (prostration)

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless. (prostration)

prayers.title: Ending: Glory, both now, without prostrations
prayers.content:
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless.

Without prostrations.

prayers.title: Prayer of forgiveness: Remit, pardon
prayers.content:
Bow down to the ground and say this prayer of forgiveness:

Remit, pardon and forgive, O God, our transgressions, both voluntary and involuntary, in word and in deed, in knowledge and in ignorance, in mind and in thought, by day and by night: forgive me them all, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Prayer: Forgive them that hate and wrong us
prayers.content:
Rise and say this prayer:

Forgive them that hate and wrong us, O Lord, thou lover of mankind. Do good unto them that do good. Grant unto our brethren and all our kin, and unto them that dwell in solitude, all their petitions that are unto salvation, and life eternal. Visit and heal them that are sick. Set free them that are in prison. Be thou the pilot of them that sail upon the waters. Direct and prosper them that journey by the way. Remember, O Lord, our captive brethren of one faith with us, of the Orthodox faith, and deliver them from every evil circumstance. Have mercy, O Lord, on them that have given us alms, and have charged us, the unworthy, to pray for them: forgive them and have mercy on them. Have mercy, O Lord, on them that labor and serve us, that show us mercy and feed us, and grant them all their petitions that are unto salvation, and life eternal. Remember, O Lord, our fathers and brethren that have departed before us, and make them to dwell where the light of thy countenance shineth. Remember also, O Lord, our lowliness and poverty, and enlighten our mind with the light of the knowledge of thy holy Gospel, and guide us in the path of thy commandments; through the prayers of thy most pure Mother and of all thy saints. Amen.

prayers.title: Cell rule: the twelve opening prostrations
prayers.content:
Stand in your usual place. With humility of heart and a contrite mind, make prostrations to the ground, saying:

O God, cleanse me a sinner, and have mercy on me. (prostration)

Thou who hast created me, O Lord, have mercy on me. (prostration)

Without number have I sinned; O Lord, forgive me. (prostration)

O God, be merciful to me a sinner. (prostration)

O God, forgive my iniquities and transgressions. (prostration)

O my most holy Lady, God-bearer, have mercy on me and save me, and help me now in this life, and at the departure of my soul, and in the age to come. (prostration)

O invincible and divine power of the honorable and life-giving Cross of the Lord, forsake me not, a sinner who hopeth in thee. (prostration)

All ye heavenly powers, holy angels and archangels, cherubim and seraphim, have mercy on me, and pray for me unto the Lord God, and help me now in this life, and at the departure of my soul, and in the age to come. (prostration)

O angel of Christ, my holy guardian, have mercy on me, and pray for me a sinner unto the Lord God, and help me now in this life, and at the departure of my soul, and in the age to come. (prostration)

O holy and great John, prophet and forerunner of the Lord, have mercy on me, and pray for me unto the Lord God, and help me now in this life, and at the departure of my soul, and in the age to come. (prostration)

O holy and glorious apostles, prophets and martyrs, hierarchs, venerable and righteous ones, and all ye saints, have mercy on me, and pray for me a sinner unto the Lord God, and help me now in this life, and at the departure of my soul, and in the age to come. (prostration)

O Lord, whether in word, or in deed, or in thought I have sinned in all my life, have mercy on me and forgive me, for thy mercy's sake. (prostration)

prayers.title: Prayer of St Macarius
prayers.content:
The prayer of Saint Macarius.

O God, cleanse me a sinner, for I have never done any good thing before thee; but deliver me from the evil one, and let thy will be done in me; that without condemnation I may open my unworthy mouth, and praise thy holy name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of St Isaac the Syrian
prayers.content:
The second prayer, of Saint Isaac the Syrian.

O Lord Jesus Christ my God, who visitest thy creation: my passions are manifest unto thee, and the weakness of my nature, and the strength of mine adversary. Do thou thyself, O Master, shield me from his malice; for his strength is mighty, and my nature is subject to passion, and my strength is feeble. Thou therefore who art good, who knowest my weakness and bearest the burden of my feebleness, keep me from troubled thoughts and from the flood of the passions, and make me worthy of this holy service; lest by my passions I corrupt the sweetness thereof, and be found shameless and presumptuous before thee. But in thy mercy have mercy upon me; for blessed art thou unto the ages. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of St Stephen of Thebes
prayers.content:
The third prayer, of Saint Stephen of Thebes.

O Master, Lord Jesus Christ my God, be thou my helper, for I am in thy hands. Suffer me not to sin, for I am led astray. Suffer me not to follow mine evil will. Suffer me not to perish in my sins. Have compassion on thy creature. Cast me not away from thy face because of my sins, for unto thee have I fled. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee. Before thee are all they that afflict me, and that seek after my soul to take it; and I have no other refuge but thee alone, O Lord. O Lord, save me for thy mercy's sake, for thou, O Lord, art mighty in all things. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of St John Chrysostom
prayers.content:
The fourth prayer, of Saint John Chrysostom.

O Lord, whether I will or no, save me. For I, as mire that loveth filth, desire the defilement of sin; but thou, being good and almighty, canst restrain me. For if thou have mercy upon the righteous, it is no great thing; and if thou save the pure, it is no marvel, for they are worthy of thy mercy. But upon me, O Master, the wretched and sinful and defiled, show forth the wonder of thy mercy, and make manifest thy loving-kindness; for unto thee am I left, a beggar, made poor of all good works. O Lord, save me for thy mercy's sake, for blessed art thou unto the ages. Amen.

prayers.title: The fifth prayer of the cell rule
prayers.content:
The fifth prayer.

O Master, have mercy on me for thy goodness' sake, and suffer me not to stray from thy will. And turn not away my poor prayer from thy face, but hear, O Lord, the voice of my prayer when I pray unto thee by day and by night, and receive it as choice incense. And because of my sins withhold not thy grace, but save me for the sake of thy holy name. For thine alone it is to have mercy on us and to save us, and unto thee we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: Blessing with the cross
prayers.content:
Having prayed and first cleansed yourself, kiss the cross that you wear on your breast, sign yourself with it, and say:

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, bless and sanctify and preserve me by the power of thy life-giving Cross.

prayers.title: Prayers to the God-bearer
prayers.content:
Then make 100 waist bows with the prayer:

My most holy Lady, God-bearer, save me a sinner.

With the shorter forms of the rule: 100 prayers to the God-bearer with 200 prostrations, or 50 with 100.

prayers.title: It is truly meet
prayers.content: It is truly meet to bless thee, O God-bearer, ever blessed and most immaculate, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify.

prayers.title: Troparia: Have mercy on us, O Lord
prayers.content:
Troparia, Tone 6.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for, being at a loss for any defense, this prayer do we sinners offer unto thee as Master: have mercy on us.

Glory: O Lord, have mercy on us, for in thee have we put our trust. Be not exceeding wroth with us, neither remember our iniquities; but look upon us as one compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies. For thou art our God, and we are thy people; we are all the work of thy hands, and we call upon thy name.

Both now: Open unto us the doors of compassion, O blessed God-bearer and Virgin, that hoping in thee we perish not, but through thee may be delivered from adversities; for thou art the salvation of the Christian race.

prayers.title: Ending of the cell rule
prayers.content:
Lord, have mercy. (forty times)

More honorable than the cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, true God-bearer, thee do we magnify.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, bless.

Three prostrations.

prayers.title: Dismissal: venerable fathers
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: venerable fathers (Sunday)
prayers.content: O Thou who didst rise from the dead: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: Sunday at Matins and the Hours
prayers.content: O Thou who didst rise from the dead: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, by the power of the honorable and life-giving Cross, and of the holy, glorious and all-praised apostles, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: bodiless powers (Monday)
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and through the intercession of the honorable heavenly bodiless powers, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: the Forerunner (Tuesday)
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of the honorable and glorious prophet, forerunner and baptist John, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: the Cross (Wednesday and Friday)
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, by the power of the honorable and life-giving Cross, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: the apostles (Thursday; Sunday Vespers)
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of the holy, glorious and all-praised apostles, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: all the saints (Saturday)
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, by the power of the honorable and life-giving Cross, through the intercession of the honorable heavenly bodiless powers, and of the honorable and glorious prophet, forerunner and baptist John, and of the holy, glorious and all-praised apostles, and of the holy and right-victorious martyrs, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of the holy and righteous ancestors of God, Joachim and Anna, and of Saint N., to whom the church is dedicated, and of [saint], whose day it is, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: a great saint or the church's saint
prayers.content:
When the feast of the church's saint, or the memory of a great saint, takes the place of the weekday dismissal:

O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of [saint], whose memory we keep, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal for one who has died
prayers.content: O Thou who hast dominion over the living and the dead: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother and of all the saints, give rest to the soul of thy departed servant N. (or: of thy departed handmaid N.) in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in the abodes of the righteous; and have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal for those who have died
prayers.content: O Thou who hast dominion over the living and the dead: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother and of all the saints, give rest to the souls of thy departed servants, our fathers and brethren N., in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in the abodes of the righteous; and have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal for the Universal Saturday
prayers.content: O Thou who hast dominion over the living and the dead: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother and of all the saints, give rest to the souls of those who have fallen asleep before us and are ever remembered, our blessed founders, fathers and brethren, who lie here, and of Orthodox Christians everywhere, in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in the abodes of the righteous; and have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Saturday after the canon: for one who has died
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of all the saints, have mercy on and give rest to the soul of thy servant N. (or: of thy departed handmaid N.) unto the endless ages, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Saturday after the canon: for those who have died
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of all the saints, have mercy on and give rest to the souls of thy servants, our fathers and brethren, unto the endless ages, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Saturday after the canon: the general universal dismissal
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of our venerable and God-bearing fathers, and of all the saints, have mercy on and give rest to the souls of those who have fallen asleep before us and are ever remembered, our blessed founders, fathers and brethren, who lie here, and of Orthodox Christians everywhere, unto the endless ages, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Vespers
prayers.content: After finishing the kathismas or the lestovkas of Jesus Prayers, pray to the most holy God-bearer as much as you are able and wish: a lestovka, or 50 prostrations, or 12. Do the same for the saints who fall on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Vespers on Saturday evening
prayers.content: After finishing the kathismas or the lestovkas of Jesus Prayers, pray to the most holy God-bearer as much as you are able and wish: a lestovka, or 50 prostrations, or 12. Do the same for the saints who fall on that date. On Saturday, pray to the Cross and the Resurrection.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Vespers of a feast
prayers.content: After finishing the kathismas or the lestovkas of Jesus Prayers, pray to the most holy God-bearer as much as you are able and wish: a lestovka, or 50 prostrations, or 12. Do the same for the saints who fall on that date. On a feast, pray to the feast.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Compline
prayers.content: After the kathisma or the lestovkas, pray to the God-bearer as your strength allows, in place of her canon. Laypeople who do not always pray the rule should pray to the guardian angel after the prostrations to the God-bearer.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Compline on Friday evening
prayers.content:
On Friday evening, when it is not a feast, make as many prostrations as you wish in place of the canon for the departed, before the prostrations to the God-bearer.

After the kathisma or the lestovkas, pray to the God-bearer as your strength allows, in place of her canon. Laypeople who do not always pray the rule should pray to the guardian angel after the prostrations to the God-bearer.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Midnight Office
prayers.content: Make some prostrations for the reposed: 12, or fewer, or more.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Sunday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray first to the Cross and the Resurrection, and after that to the God-bearer. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Monday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray to the God-bearer and to the archangels. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Tuesday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray to the God-bearer and to the Forerunner. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Wednesday and Friday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray first to the honorable Cross, and after that to the God-bearer. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Thursday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray to the God-bearer and to the apostles and Nicholas. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins on Saturday
prayers.content: After the kathismas, pray to the God-bearer and to all the saints. Pray also to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: Matins of a great feast of the Lord on a Sunday
prayers.content: When a great feast of the Lord falls on a Sunday, do not pray to the Resurrection; pray to the feast. After that, pray to the God-bearer, and to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: the Hours
prayers.content: After the kathismas, make as many prostrations to the God-bearer as you wish, and pray to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: the Hours on Sunday
prayers.content: On Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, after the kathismas or lestovkas, pray first to the Resurrection, and then to the God-bearer and to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Daily additions: the Hours of a great feast of the Lord on a Sunday
prayers.content: When a great feast of the Lord falls on a Sunday, do not pray to the Resurrection; after the kathismas or lestovkas, pray first to the feast, and then to the God-bearer and to the saint who falls on that date.

prayers.title: Dismissal: Sep 1, the Indiction
prayers.content: O Thou who by thine almighty and ineffable wisdom didst establish the beginning of the indiction, that is, of the new year: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of her honorable and glorious synaxis in Miasena; and of our venerable father Symeon the Stylite and archimandrite, and of his mother Martha; and of the holy martyr Aithalas; and of the holy forty women, and of holy Ammon the deacon, their teacher; and of the holy martyrs Callistus, Evodus and Hermogenes, brothers according to the flesh; and of Joshua the son of Nun, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: Sep 6, the Archangel Michael
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and through the intercession of the holy and great captain of the hosts, the Archistrategos Michael, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Dismissal: Sep 8, the Nativity of the God-bearer
prayers.content: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, for the prayers of thy most pure Mother, and of her honorable and glorious Nativity, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for thou art good and the lover of mankind.

prayers.title: Fasting: Great Lent
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32, fol. 74

In the first week, called Theodore's week, fast for two days, Monday and Tuesday, neither eating bread nor drinking water, and devote yourself to prayer and prostrations. On Wednesday, after the dismissal of vespers, at the ninth hour of the day, we eat dry food and raw vegetables and drink hot water with honey. Then fast again until Friday. On Friday eat bread, raw vegetables, and cooked food without relish.

On the weak. Anyone who is weak, or cannot fast for two days, should eat bread with water on Tuesday, and likewise on Thursday.

On the old. Anyone who is very old, worn out by illness, or very young should eat bread with water on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

On Saturday and Sunday. On Saturday and Sunday we eat cooked food with oil.

Lenten Triodion, fol. 140, and the Psalter with Appendices

On the other days of the holy fast, cooked food is not eaten on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. On Tuesday and Thursday cooked food is eaten.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: Great Lent
prayers.content:
The typikon of the Holy Mountain

According to the typikon of the Holy Mountain, one should not eat at all on the first day. On Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday one should eat a pound of bread a day, with water, and nothing else except salt. In his catechesis for Friday of the first week, St Theodore the Studite praises eating every day at the appointed hour.

Nomocanon, rule 220

In holy and great Lent we eat once a day, dry food only: legumes without oil. We take wine and oil on Saturday and Sunday, and shellfish likewise. Fish we eat only on the Annunciation and on Palm Sunday.

Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 24

First week: On Monday, Wednesday and Friday no table is set. On Tuesday and Thursday the brethren are given white bread, a stewed-fruit drink with honey, cloudberries or sauerkraut, and oat meal stirred into water. On Saturday: white cabbage soup, pea noodles and porridge with seed milk, all with oil. On Sunday: salted fish fillets with the cabbage soup, and porridge.

The other weeks: On Monday, Wednesday and Friday, two cold dishes with the cabbage soup. On Tuesday and Thursday, beet soup with seed milk, rusks, one cold dish and one hot. On Saturday and Sunday, salted fish fillets or air-cured fish with the cabbage soup, and porridge.

Wednesday of the fourth week. At the brethren's table, three hot dishes without oil.

Thursday of the fifth week. At table we eat with oil and drink wine because of the labor of the vigil.

Saturday of righteous Lazarus. At table we eat cooked food with oil, and caviar if there is any, and drink wine.

Palm Sunday. A consolation at the brethren's table: we eat fish and drink wine, giving thanks to God.

prayers.title: Fasting: Holy Week
prayers.content:
On the Christian Life, fol. 85, and the Psalter with Appendices, fol. 373-374

During Holy Week, for six days from Monday until Saturday evening, eat only bread with water and uncooked vegetables, and that with restraint. If possible, do not take food every day, as was said of the first week. On holy and great Friday eat nothing. On Great Saturday likewise we are commanded to fast until the third hour of the night. Then, after the divine liturgy is completed, taste a little bread with water and drink one cup of wine.

On holy and great Thursday we eat cooked food without oil and drink wine; otherwise the food is dry. For the Council of Laodicea, speaking of Great Thursday in canon 44, says that it is not right to break the fast on the Thursday of the last week of Lent and so dishonor the whole of Lent.

On Great Friday, if it is possible, one should not eat, as the fathers command. Yet we do not hold this as a strict rule that nothing at all is eaten then, since the fathers set it according to each person's strength. So if you can, keep the fast on these two days, Friday and Saturday; this is good and well-pleasing. If not, keep it at least on Saturday. On Friday eat bread and raw vegetables and drink water, but each as he wishes and is able.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: Holy Week
prayers.content:
Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 24

In Holy Week a table is set on Monday and Wednesday for those who wish to eat; they eat three cold dishes. On Tuesday: cabbage, berries and oat meal. On Thursday: cabbage soup, pea noodles and porridge with seed milk, all without oil. On Great Friday neither the brethren nor the laypeople eat. On Great Saturday, after the dismissal of the liturgy, the brethren are given pieces of bread.

prayers.title: Fasting: Bright Week
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

We command every Christian to eat cheese, eggs, milk and meat after holy Pascha, through that whole week from Bright Sunday to Thomas Sunday, and we drink with moderation.

prayers.title: Fasting: From Thomas Sunday to Pentecost
prayers.content:
The Home Ustav

From Thomas Sunday until the Descent of the Holy Spirit there is no fasting and no prostrations. If you wish to abstain from drink and fish on Wednesday and Friday, that is left to your own will.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: From Thomas Sunday to Pentecost
prayers.content:
On the Christian Life

From Thomas Sunday until the Descent of the Holy Spirit there is no fasting and no kneeling. If anyone wishes to abstain from fish and wine on Wednesday and Friday, that is left to each person's will.

Nomocanon, rule 224

Throughout all of Pentecost, Wednesdays and Fridays are released for fish, oil and wine. If dry eating is released on such days, it is at the ninth hour, and that is left to each person's choice.

Great Typikon, ch. 32

From Monday of New Week, throughout Pentecost, on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, after the third and sixth hours have been sung, together with the typika, the brethren are given a blessing of two ounces of plain rusks. This alone is to be eaten, in the narthex, for the sake of Pentecost, so that it is not called a fast. After the ninth hour has been sung at its proper time, they then eat a full meal, according to the tradition of the holy fathers.

Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 29

From Thomas Sunday, throughout Pentecost, on Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, a table is set twice, with fish. On Monday, a table once, with fish. On Wednesday and Friday, a table once, and we eat dried fish. On Mid-Pentecost Wednesday and at the leave-taking of Pascha, a table once, with fish.

prayers.title: Fasting: The week after Pentecost
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32, and On the Christian Life

On the Sunday of the Descent of the Holy Spirit there is kneeling at vespers. That week is a fast-free week. On Wednesday and Friday you may eat cheese, eggs, milk and meat, and drink with moderation, until All Saints' Sunday.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: The week after Pentecost
prayers.content:
Solovetsky

Throughout this week they eat cheese, eggs and fish, and the laypeople eat meat. There is supper every day.

prayers.title: Fasting: The Fast of the Holy Apostles
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

You should know that in the fast of the holy apostles, in the fast of Christ's Nativity, and in the fast of the Dormition of the Most Holy God-bearer, we do not eat fish on Tuesday and Thursday, only oil and wine. On Monday, Wednesday and Friday we take neither oil nor wine. We fast until the ninth hour and eat once on those days, with dry eating.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: The Fast of the Holy Apostles
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 34

In the fast before Christ's Nativity and in the fast of the holy apostles, monks are commanded not to eat fish except on Saturday and Sunday. Laypeople may eat fish twice a day on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

Nomocanon, rule 223

In the fast of the holy apostles, of Christ's Nativity and of the God-bearer, we keep dry eating three days a week, that is, Monday, Wednesday and Friday. We abstain from fish, oil and wine, except in sickness, and eat legumes without oil, as in Great Lent. Those who wish to please God take fish and oil only on Saturday and Sunday.

Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 29

In the fast of the holy apostles, and in the fast of Christ's Nativity until St Nicholas's Day, they eat fish on Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday. On Saturday and Sunday they eat twice a day, on Tuesday and Thursday once a day. On Monday: two hot dishes and a third cold one. On Wednesday and Friday: two cold dishes and a third hot one.

Matthew's Syntagma of Canons, from the canons of Patriarch Nikephoros, rule 19

In the fast of the holy apostles and of St Philip, monks living in the monastery should eat once, toward evening, on Wednesday and Friday. Those who work should eat after the sixth hour and take supper in the evening.

prayers.title: Fasting: The Fast of the Most Holy God-bearer
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

In the fifteen-day fast of our Most Holy Lady the God-bearer before the Dormition, except on the Transfiguration of Christ, we fast until the ninth hour of the day. On Monday, Wednesday and Friday we eat dry food and make prostrations until communion. On Tuesday and Thursday we eat cooked food without oil. On Saturday and Sunday we eat cooked food with oil and drink wine.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: The Fast of the Most Holy God-bearer
prayers.content:
On the Christian Life, and the Nomocanon, fol. 83

The fast of our Most Pure Lady the God-bearer is kept with dry eating, as described before. On Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday oil and drink are allowed, but no fish at all except on the Lord's Transfiguration. The other days are kept with dry eating and prostrations until communion, as was said for the fast of the holy apostles.

Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 29

In the fast of the Most Holy God-bearer, on the first day, the Procession of the Cross, they eat cabbage soup, pea noodles with oil and porridge with seed milk, once a day. If it falls on a Saturday or Sunday, they eat twice a day. On the Transfiguration of the Lord and on the memory of the Solovetsky wonderworkers they eat fish twice a day. On the other days of the weeks it is as in the fast of Christ's Nativity after St Nicholas's Day, with salted fish fillets on Saturday and Sunday.

prayers.title: Fasting: The Nativity Fast, to St Nicholas
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

From the day of the holy apostle Philip until the day of our holy father Nicholas, eat dry food on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. On Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday we eat fish. From the day of our holy father Nicholas until Christ's Nativity we eat fish on Saturday and Sunday, and on Tuesday and Thursday cooked food with oil, and we drink wine.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: The Nativity Fast, to St Nicholas
prayers.content:
Nomocanon, fol. 83, and On the Christian Life

In the holy fast before Christ's Nativity we allow fish only on Saturday and Sunday, and oil and wine on Tuesday and Thursday. On Monday, Wednesday and Friday we fast until the ninth hour. If anyone cannot drink only water on Monday, he may allow himself oil and wine. Wednesday and Friday should be kept as far as one's strength allows, except in serious and grave illness.

Solovetsky Typikon, ch. 29

In the fast of Christ's Nativity, until the day of St Nicholas the Wonderworker, they eat fish on Saturday, Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday: twice on Saturday and Sunday, once a day on Tuesday and Thursday. On Monday, with the cabbage soup, one cold dish and one hot. On Wednesday and Friday, with the cabbage soup, two cold dishes. From St Nicholas's Day until the forefeast of Christ's Nativity: on Saturday and Sunday, salted fish fillets. On Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with the cabbage soup, two cold dishes. On Tuesday and Thursday, with the cabbage soup, one cold dish and one hot.

On the forefeast of Christ's Nativity, on Saturday and Sunday they eat with oil, twice a day. On the other days it is as in Great Lent.

prayers.title: Fasting: The Twelve Days
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

From Christ's Nativity until the day of holy Theophany, eat cheese, eggs, milk and meat on Wednesday and Friday, as on any other day. From the Baptism of the Lord until the Publican and Pharisee, eat fish on Wednesday and Friday.

prayers.title: Fasting: From Theophany to the Publican and Pharisee
prayers.content:
On the Christian Life

From the Baptism of the Lord until the week of the Publican and Pharisee, fast on Wednesday and Friday.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: From Theophany to the Publican and Pharisee
prayers.content:
Great Typikon, ch. 32

From Christ's Nativity until the day of holy Theophany, eat cheese, eggs, milk and meat on Wednesday and Friday, as on any other day. From the Baptism of the Lord until the Publican and Pharisee, eat fish on Wednesday and Friday.

prayers.title: Fasting: The Week of the Publican and Pharisee
prayers.content:
Great Typikon

The week of the Publican and Pharisee is called Artsiburius week, in which the accursed Armenians fast. But for us Christians it is released by the canons of the holy fathers. On Wednesday and Friday we eat cheese, eggs, milk, oil and meat, to curse the Armenian heresy.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: The Week of the Publican and Pharisee
prayers.content:
Ancient Kirillov Typikon

Throughout the week of the Pharisee there is supper every day.

prayers.title: Fasting: From the Prodigal Son to Meatfare Sunday
prayers.content:
The Sergiev and Kirillov Typikon, manuscript (Patriarchal Library in Moscow, no. 504), fol. 175

On the other days, from the Sunday of the Prodigal until Meatfare Sunday, keep everything without change as described for the other days of the Pharisee's week. Only throughout the Prodigal's week, dry eating is kept on the fast days.

prayers.title: Fasting: Cheesefare Week
prayers.content:
Typikon

Likewise, for Cheesefare week the holy council commanded eating cheese, eggs and fish. On Wednesday and Friday, eat once a day at the ninth hour, after the hours have been sung with vespers, because of the Andonian, Sabellian and many other heretics, whom we curse.

prayers.title: Fasting, other typika: Cheesefare Week
prayers.content:
Solovetsky, Sergiev and Kirillov

On Monday of Cheesefare week we eat twice a day. On Wednesday and Friday there is no supper.

prayers.title: Fasting: Wednesdays and Fridays through the year
prayers.content:
Nikon of the Black Mountain, ch. 57, and On the Christian Life

From the fast of the holy apostles until the memory of the holy apostle Philip, and throughout the whole year, apart from the appointed fasts and the fast-free days, lay people are to keep two days of every week as fasts, Wednesday and Friday. These two days are kept as in holy Great Lent: no fish, oil or wine. Whoever chooses also to abstain from meat on Monday does well. But at the very least, every Christian is bound to fast on Wednesday and Friday without fail, as the divine apostles laid down in canon 69, saying:

If any bishop, presbyter, deacon, subdeacon, reader or singer does not fast during the forty days, that is, Great Lent, or on every Wednesday and Friday throughout the year, let him be deposed, unless bodily illness prevents him. For the sick are permitted to take oil and wine according to their strength. If a layman does not fast, let him be excommunicated.

See the Kormchaya, fol. 19.

So the divine apostles established and decreed. After them the holy fathers, assembled at Gangra by the Divine Spirit, spoke together concerning all the fasts established by the holy apostles and those decreed afterward. With full authority, in canon 18, they gave this fearful ruling:

If any of those who practice abstinence, without bodily need, becomes proud and breaks the fasts handed down for common observance and kept by the Church, as though his own reasoning were firm and complete, let him be anathema.

See the Kormchaya, fol. 59.

And Apollos, great among the fathers, calls it the most fearful of all sins to break the fasts of the Church without any need. For on Wednesday Christ was betrayed, and on Friday He was crucified. Whoever breaks these days betrays the Saviour and joins in crucifying Him. Likewise St Athanasius the Great says: "Whoever breaks Wednesday and Friday crucifies the Lord, as the Jews did. For on Wednesday they took counsel against Him, and on Friday they crucified Him." The only exceptions are the Theophany days, Pentecost, and the weeks released by the Church. Likewise, whoever eats freely on feasts is not guilty.

Nikephoros, Patriarch of Constantinople, says in his fifth canon that one should not receive communion from a priest who does not fast on Wednesday and Friday. See the Nomocanon, rule 214.

When and where the Wednesday and Friday fast is released: Nomocanon, rule 224, and the Book of Faith, fol. 126

Know this as well. Throughout the whole year, the Wednesday and Friday fast is released for fish on the Lord's feasts and the feasts of the God-bearer. But if the eve of such a feast falls on a Wednesday or Friday, the fast is not released that evening, even though tomorrow is the feast. Throughout Pentecost, Wednesdays and Fridays are released for fish, oil and wine. If dry eating is released on such days, it is at the ninth hour, and that is left to each person's choice.

On feasts of the holy apostles, holy martyrs and holy hierarchs falling on a Wednesday or Friday, we do not release the fast for fish, only for oil and wine and nothing more, though at the superior's discretion it is not forbidden. We eat fish on the Nativity of the Forerunner, but on his other feasts not at all, only oil and wine. Likewise on the day of the chief apostles Peter and Paul we allow fish.

But above all, whoever wishes to be saved should keep every Wednesday and Friday of the whole year with dry eating and drinking water, according to the 69th canon of the holy apostles. If anyone cannot do so because of bodily weakness, let him allow himself wine only. Even that should be done with contrition of heart, keeping away from fish and oil altogether. Whoever also abstains from wine will find a reward as a keeper of the commandment.
